newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds shed Brazil worries to close firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds shed Brazil worries to close firm.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed firm Wednesday with big institutional buying reinforcing a technical rebound, and encouragement from a YPF share sale and from U.S. Treasuries, dealers said.
"With instituational investors participating once again, the market began climbing once more on the good perspectives for the medium term," said dealer Jose Salgado.
The market rebounded early from Tuesday's losses on fears that Brazil could devalue, and was helped along by gains for U.S. Treasuries on good U.S. inflation figures.

With enthusiasm dampened by the confirmation of reports that Argentina would delay the issue of a $750 million global bond because of volatile emerging markets, the sale of the 10 percent of YPF shares in staff hands was seen as good news.

"The placing of the YPF shares at $29.25 was considered a good signal, since although it was lower than what the market wanted expectations had been lowered by the Brazilian devaluation rumors," said another dealer.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 0.35 percent at $94.35 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was unchanged at 118.20.
